options.B: [latex]x_{1}(t) \; and \; x_{2}(t)[/latex] are real and [latex]x_{1}(t) x_{2}(t)[/latex] is also real
options.C: [latex]x_{1}(t) \; and \; x_{2}(t)[/latex] are complex but [latex]x_{1}(t) x_{2}(t)[/latex] is real
options.D: [latex]x_{1}(t) \; and \; x_{2}(t)[/latex] are imaginary but [latex]x_{1}(t) x_{2}(t)[/latex] is real

questions.explanation: By observing [latex]X_1(j \omega )[/latex] and [latex]X_2(j \omega )[/latex], we can say that they are not conjugate symmetric. Since, the fourier transform is not conjugate symmetric the signal will not be real. So, [latex]x_1(t), x_2(t)[/latex] are not real. Now the fourier transform of [latex]x_1(t) \cdot x_2(t)[/latex] will be [latex]\frac{1}{2\pi}X_1(j \omega )*X_2(j \omega )[/latex] and by looking at [latex]X_1(j \omega )[/latex] and [latex]X_2(j \omega )[/latex], we can say that [latex]X_1(j \omega ) *X_2(j \omega )[/latex] will be conjugate symmetric and thus [latex]x_1(t) \cdot x_2(t)[/latex] will be real. By observing [latex]X_1(j \omega )[/latex] and [latex]X_2(j \omega )[/latex], we can say, [latex]X_2( \omega )=X_1(- \omega )\overset{IFT}{\rightarrow}x_2(t)=x_1(-t)\;\;...(i)[/latex] Now, [latex]X_1(j \omega )[/latex] is real. Therefore, [latex]x_1(t)[/latex] will be conjugate symmetric. [latex]\begin{aligned} \text{i.e., } x_1(t)&=x_1^*(-t) \\ \downarrow t&= -t\\ x_1(-t)&= x_1^*(t)\\ \text{Now, }x_1(t)\cdot x_2(t) &= x_1(t)\cdot x_1(-t) \;\;(from \;(i))\\ &= x_1(t)\cdot x_1^*(t)\\ &= |x_1(t)|^2=\text{real function} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: The open loop transfer function of a unity feedback control system is given by [latex]G(s)=\frac{K(s+1)}{s(1+Ts)(1+2s)}, K\gt 0,T \gt 0[/latex] The closed loop system will be stable if,
questions.explanation: Open loop transfer function: [latex]G(s)=\frac{K(s+1)}{s(1+Ts)(1+2s)};[/latex]  [latex] \; K \gt 0 \; [/latex] and [latex]\; t \gt 0[/latex] For closed loop system stability, characteristic equation is, [latex]1+G(s)H(s)=0[/latex] [latex] 1+\frac{K(s+1)}{s(1+Ts)(1+2s)}\cdot 1=0[/latex] [latex] s(1+Ts)(1+2s)+K(s+1)=0 [/latex] [latex]2Ts^3+(2+T)s^2+(1+K)s+K=0 [/latex] Using Routh's criteria, For stability, [latex]K \gt 0[/latex] and  [latex] (2+T)(1+K)-2TK \gt 0 [/latex] [latex]K(2+T-2T)+(2+T) \gt 0 [/latex] or [latex] -(T-2)K+2(2+T) \gt 0 [/latex] [latex]-K \gt -\frac{(2+T)}{(T-2)}[/latex] or  [latex] K \lt \frac{T+2}{(T-2)} [/latex] Hence for stability, [latex]0 \lt K \lt \frac{T+2}{T-2}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
Open loop transfer function:
[latex]G(s)=\frac{K(s+1)}{s(1+Ts)(1+2s)};[/latex] [latex] \; K \gt 0 \; [/latex] and [latex]\; t \gt 0[/latex]
For closed loop system stability, characteristic equation is,
[latex]1+G(s)H(s)=0[/latex]
[latex] 1+\frac{K(s+1)}{s(1+Ts)(1+2s)}\cdot 1=0[/latex]
[latex] s(1+Ts)(1+2s)+K(s+1)=0 [/latex]
[latex]2Ts^3+(2+T)s^2+(1+K)s+K=0 [/latex]
Using Routh's criteria,

For stability, [latex]K \gt 0[/latex]
and [latex] (2+T)(1+K)-2TK \gt 0 [/latex]
[latex]K(2+T-2T)+(2+T) \gt 0 [/latex]
or
[latex] -(T-2)K+2(2+T) \gt 0 [/latex]
[latex]-K \gt -\frac{(2+T)}{(T-2)}[/latex] or [latex] K \lt \frac{T+2}{(T-2)} [/latex]
Hence for stability,
[latex]0 \lt K \lt \frac{T+2}{T-2}[/latex]

questions.question: The gain at the breakaway point of the root locus of a unity feedback system with open loop transfer function [latex]G(s)=\frac{Ks}{(s-1)(s-4)}[/latex] is

[latex]OLTS\Rightarrow G(s)=\frac{Ks}{(s-1)(s-4)}[/latex]
Now, characteristic equation,
[latex]1+G(s)H(s)=0[/latex]
[latex] \frac{Ks}{(s-1)(s-4)}+1=0[/latex]

[latex]\;\;K=-\frac{(s^2-5s+4)}{s}=\left [ s-5+\frac{4}{s} \right ][/latex]
